record.paper_title: Stability of Homomorphisms, Coverings and Cocycles II: Examples, Applications and Open Problems
record.context_brief: locally testable codes with permutation coefficients
record.original_question: Given a binary linear code Ker(A) defined by a matrix A and the associated presentation of F2^k generated by involution, commutation, and linear relations coming from A, what can be proved about the homomorphism stability rate of this presentation when the test maps are allowed to take values in arbitrary symmetric groups Sym(n), rather than being restricted to Sym(2)? In particular, what happens for presentations coming from Reed-Muller codes or from recently constructed good locally testable codes?

evidence.quote:
Problem 6.11 (Locally testable codes with permutation coefficients). Given a matrix A ∈ Mm×n(F2), one can
define the following presentation of Fk2, where k = n − rank(A):

What about the case where the inputs are not restricted to be with range Sym(2), but any Sym(n)? Namely, what can be said about the homomorphism stability rate of the above presentation for a given code? For the Hadamard code the resulting presentation is essentially the multiplication table of Fk2, and is thus stable but expansive. What about more reasonably sized codes, such as Reed–Muller codes? Or, the recently constructed good locally testable codes [DEL+22,PK22]?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}_2 = \{0,1\}$ and let $A \in M_{m \times n}(\mathbb{F}_2)$ be a binary matrix whose row $A_i$ has entries $A_{i,1},\dots,A_{i,n}$. Set $k = n - \mathrm{rank}(A)$, so that the binary linear code $\mathrm{Ker}(A) \le \mathbb{F}_2^n$ surjects onto $\mathbb{F}_2^k$. Associate with $A$ the following finite presentation of the group $\mathbb{F}_2^k$:
\[
\mathcal{P}(A) \;=\; \Big\langle\, x_1,\dots,x_n \;\Big|\; x_j^2=e\ (1\le j\le n),\ \ [x_i,x_j]=e\ (1\le i<j\le n),\ \ \prod_{j=1}^{n} x_j^{A_{i,j}} = e\ (1\le i\le m)\,\Big\rangle.
\]

For an integer $N\ge 1$, let $\mathrm{Sym}(N)$ be the symmetric group on $N$ letters equipped with the normalized Hamming distance $d_H(\sigma,\tau) = \frac{1}{N}\#\{x : \sigma(x)\ne \tau(x)\}$. A map $f : \{x_1,\dots,x_n\} \to \mathrm{Sym}(N)$ extends multiplicatively to evaluate every relator $r$ as an element $f(r) \in \mathrm{Sym}(N)$. Define the local defect
\[
\mathrm{loc}(f) \;=\; \max_{r \in R}\, d_H\!\big(f(r),\mathrm{id}\big),
\]
where $R$ is the set of relators in $\mathcal{P}(A)$, and the global defect
\[
\mathrm{glob}(f) \;=\; \inf_{\varphi}\, \max_{1\le j\le n} d_H\!\big(f(x_j),\varphi(x_j)\big),
\]
where the infimum is over all group homomorphisms $\varphi : \mathbb{F}_2^k \to \mathrm{Sym}(N)$ (precomposed with the canonical map sending $x_j$ to its image in $\mathbb{F}_2^k$). The homomorphism stability rate of $\mathcal{P}(A)$ (with respect to $\mathrm{Sym}(N)$ test maps, $N$ arbitrary) is the function
\[
\rho_A(\varepsilon) \;=\; \sup\big\{\,\mathrm{glob}(f) \;:\; N\ge 1,\ f:\{x_j\}\to\mathrm{Sym}(N),\ \mathrm{loc}(f)\le \varepsilon\,\big\}.
\]

Problem. Determine the behavior of $\rho_A(\varepsilon)$ as $\varepsilon \to 0^+$ for natural families of matrices $A$. In particular:

(a) For $A$ the parity-check matrix of a Reed–Muller code $\mathrm{RM}(r,t)$ over $\mathbb{F}_2$, give quantitative bounds on $\rho_A$ (linear, polynomial, or otherwise), and determine whether the resulting presentation is homomorphism stable, and if so with what rate.

(b) For $A$ the parity-check matrix of a family of asymptotically good locally testable codes (codes of linear rate, linear distance, and constant query soundness), determine whether the associated presentations $\mathcal{P}(A)$ are homomorphism stable when tested against arbitrary symmetric groups $\mathrm{Sym}(N)$, and quantify the rate.

(Note: When $A$ is the parity-check matrix of the Hadamard code, $\mathcal{P}(A)$ is essentially the multiplication table of $\mathbb{F}_2^k$, which is known to be stable but with exponentially large presentation size.)
artifact.category_tag: Group stability and locally testable codes
artifact.status_search_result: The question of the homomorphism stability rate of presentations arising from Reed–Muller codes or from recently constructed asymptotically good locally testable codes (e.g., Dinur–Evra–Livne–Lubotzky–Mozes, Panteleev–Kalachev), with test maps into arbitrary symmetric groups, appears to be an open problem; available surveys and works on the connection between stability and locally testable codes treat it as a posed problem rather than a settled one.

status_evidence.title: Stability of Homomorphisms, Coverings and Cocycles I
status_evidence.snippet: Connection between homomorphism stability and local testability of error-correcting codes is discussed as a current research direction.
status_evidence.claim: The connection of stability with locally testable codes is treated as an active program, with quantitative rates for codes like Reed-Muller not pinned down.

status_evidence.title: Local Testing and Decoding of High-Rate ECCs (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Reed-Muller codes are locally testable with query complexity n^{O(1/m)}.
status_evidence.claim: While local testability parameters of Reed-Muller codes are known, the corresponding group-theoretic stability rate against arbitrary Sym(N) is not established.
